analysis.title: Is The AI Puke Finally Over? JPMorgan Says Capitulation Is "Far Along" And Tells Clients To Buy...
key_insights: JPMorgan's long momentum portfolio lagged the market by 11% in October, a roughly 6-sigma move and the worst month in a data series starting in 1985.

JPM's Lakos-Bujas now says "the capitulation process is far along" and reverses his earlier caution on momentum. He flagged momentum crowding at a 40-year high in May. His S&P 500 target stays at 8,000, about 8% above Friday's 7,377 close.
The long/short momentum factor is down 38.4% from its June peak, the deepest drawdown since ChatGPT launched. JPM's crowding gauge calls it the largest unwind since the post-GFC recovery.

In October both legs of momentum lost at once. The long side fell 12% and the short basket rallied 5%, leaving the long/short portfolio down 16%. October was also the worst month on record for Quality and Growth.

On Thursday after the midterms, momentum lagged the market by another 3% (a 7.9-sigma day), high-beta lost 7%, low-vol gained almost 6%, and the S&P fell 4.3%. The Nasdaq had its worst day since COVID.

JPM's prime desk says equity long/short leverage has fallen sharply, with its leverage index logging the biggest deleveraging since 2022. Goldman's prime book shows US fundamental L/S gross leverage down 8.7 points last week, the largest weekly decline since March 2020.

JPM's capitulation evidence: momentum crowding fell from the 100th to the 76th percentile versus 40 years of history, levered ETFs are cleaned out, CTAs are already short US equities, vol-targeting funds cut target leverage from the 65th to the 30th percentile, and sentiment moved from bullish in June to bearish.
Levered ETFs sold about $60B on Thursday, the second largest day on record, after more than $35B the prior Friday. Nomura's final count for Thursday was $48.6B.
The QQQ's RSI fell below 30 on Thursday. In the nine prior cases over three years, the QQQ gained about 4% on average over the next five sessions. The S&P was up more than 2% by midday Monday.

JPM's remaining risks: vol-control funds still have an estimated $50B of equities to sell, dealer gamma is at the 12th percentile (risks are "two-way"), retail has been hesitant since July, and corporate buybacks are being diverted to data center spending.
Goldman's overall prime book gross leverage is 314.2%, in the 85th percentile of the past year. Long sales outran short covers 5 to 1 and single stocks were sold for an eighth straight week.

The S&P forward P/E has shed about three turns since May while index-level earnings revisions were roughly flat. The 61 AI upstream stocks ($12.5T) went from 24.3x to 12.0x forward earnings in under six months.

Sub-sector forward P/E compression since May: semis 23.8x to 11.5x, GPU/ASIC makers 27.6x to 13.9x, optical networking 49.6x to 16.4x, storage hardware 21.8x to 9.0x, memory 8.0x to 3.2x. Hyperscalers fell 14% to 19.2x. Cybersecurity AI multiples rose 24% and horizontal AI 21%.

Goldman semiconductor analyst Jim Schneider calls the selloff overdone, with the SOX down 31% since October 1 and Nvidia and Broadcom at 12x and 13x 2027 earnings even with zero growth in 2028. Goldman's Jerry Shen says Samsung and SK Hynix trade below book value.

Hyperscalers booked $491B of net income over the past twelve months but free cash flow after capex was $77B, down from a $264B peak. Group buybacks fell from about $103B to $27B, and only Microsoft has repurchased stock this year.

JPM analysts forecast $1.71T of 2027 capex from the six big spenders, $397B above consensus. Each extra $100B of capex adds roughly $9 to S&P 500 EPS. Capex has beaten estimates by 29% on average since early 2024.

AI revenue per dollar of capex at the three big clouds has halved from 1.4 in early 2024 to 0.7. Backlog is 3.6x capex. JPM credit analysts say hyperscalers can fund next year barring a credit shock but will need more help from other sources including equity.

JPM's trade is long 12-month momentum versus short 3-month momentum. The 12M basket is about 34% tech (mostly semis and hardware) with a correlation near 0.8 to AI upstream names, while the 3M basket rotated into pharma and energy.
JPM warns that if semis and hardware trade sideways, they start dropping out of the 12M momentum basket in 1H27, making quant rebalancing a new source of selling in 2Q27.

JPM calls this an intra-cycle reset and "largely a deleveraging event", expects about 20% EPS growth in 2027, and lists catalysts: the Middle East, the mega-cap IPO pipeline, next month's ERCOT meeting and the December Fed.

The Zero Hedge author expects a tradeable bounce that runs into JPM's 2Q27 tripwire. The author cites moratoria that could freeze 45% of planned data center capacity and Friday's payrolls putting the Fed back on track to hike in December. Goldman's delta-one desk is quoted as betting this is 1998 and not 2000.

trade_ideas.description: Long 12-month momentum, short 3-month momentum (factor pair trade)
trade_ideas.rationale: The two baskets no longer hold the same stocks. The 12M basket is about 34% tech, mostly semis and hardware, and the 3M basket rotated into pharma and energy, so the trade buys beaten-up AI hardware against staples and energy.
trade_ideas.risk: Semis and hardware went vertical in April. If they trade sideways they drop out of the 12M basket in 1H27, and quant rebalancing becomes a source of selling in 2Q27.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM says capitulation is far along. Momentum crowding fell to the 76th percentile, levered ETFs are cleaned out, CTAs are short, and QQQ RSI below 30 has averaged about +4% over five sessions.
tension_points.bear_case: Vol-control funds still have about $50B to sell and dealer gamma is at the 12th percentile. Hyperscaler free cash flow is $77B against $491B of net income, and Goldman's prime book gross leverage is still in the 85th percentile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Semis and hardware trading sideways, which would push them out of the 12M momentum basket in 1H27 and trigger quant selling in 2Q27.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees $1.71T of 2027 capex, $397B above consensus, with each extra $100B adding about $9 to S&P 500 EPS, supporting the 8,000 target. Backlog is 3.6x capex.
tension_points.bear_case: Free cash flow is down more than two-thirds from its peak, buybacks fell to $27B, and revenue per dollar of capex halved to 0.7. JPM credit says funding needs more help from other sources including equity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A credit shock, which JPM credit analysts say is the one condition that would stop hyperscalers funding next year.
